reference.description: Reply to or forward a stored message. EmailEngine fills in the subject, the recipients and the In-Reply-To/References headers from the referenced message, and flags it as answered or forwarded once the new message is sent, so only the new content has to be supplied

message.description: EmailEngine message ID to reply to or forward

action.description: What to do with the referenced message

enumDescriptions.reply-all: Reply to the sender and every other recipient
enumDescriptions.forward: Forward the message to new recipients

action.title: MessageAction

inline.description: Quote the referenced message under the new text, the way an email client does. Without it only the new text is sent

forwardAttachments.description: Carry the attachments of the referenced message over to the forwarded copy. Only valid when action is "forward"

ignoreMissing.description: Continue sending even if the referenced message cannot be found

messageId.description: Verify the Message-ID of the referenced email matches this value before proceeding

threadId.description: Gmail thread ID to attach the outgoing message to

x-meta.usage:
Set this when you know the Gmail thread the outgoing message belongs to and do not want EmailEngine to work it out from the referenced message.

Gmail API accounts only. IMAP and MS Graph derive threading from the `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers and ignore it. When both `message` and `threadId` are given, this one wins.

mailMerge.description: Mail merge options. A separate email is generated for each recipient, up to 1000 per request

x-meta.usage:
Use this to send one personalised message per recipient in a single request, instead of one request each. Each entry gets its own queue id and its own delivery.

It takes over addressing and rendering for the whole request: `messageId`, `envelope`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc` and `render` at the message root are rejected, because each entry supplies its own.

params.title: RenderValues

mailMerge.title: MailMergeList

envelope.description: An optional object specifying the SMTP envelope used during email transmission

x-meta.usage:
Send this only when the SMTP envelope has to differ from the message headers, which in practice means variable envelope return paths, a bounce address that is not the From address, or delivering to an address that does not appear in the headers.

Left out, the envelope is derived from the headers, which is what you want for an ordinary message.

envelope.title: SMTPEnvelope

raw.description: A Base64-encoded email message in RFC 822 format

x-meta.usage:
Send `raw` when you have already built the MIME message yourself, for example when relaying something you fetched from another system, and it has to go out unchanged.

Anything else you send alongside it overrides the matching header inside it, so a `subject` sent with a raw body replaces the subject in the message. If you are composing from parts, use `text` and `html` and let EmailEngine build the MIME structure.

anyOf.description: References an existing attachment by its ID instead of providing new attachment content

x-meta.usage:
Use this to forward an attachment that is already on another message without downloading and re-uploading it. Take the id from the attachment list of the referenced message.

It is exclusive with `content`: send one or the other, never both.

trackOpens.description: Should EmailEngine track opens for this message

copy.description: If set then either copies the message to the Sent Mail folder or not. If not set then uses the account's default setting

x-meta.usage:
Leave this unset to follow the account default. Set it explicitly when one message should be filed differently from the rest, for instance an automated notification you do not want in the user Sent folder.

It only affects SMTP deliveries. Gmail and MS Graph file sent messages themselves, so the flag is a no-op there.

sentMailPath.description: Upload sent message to this folder. By default the account's Sent Mail folder is used.

deliveryAttempts.description: How many delivery attempts to make until message is considered as failed

gateway.description: Optional SMTP gateway ID for message routing

listId.description: List ID for Mail Merge. Must use a subdomain name format. Lists are registered ad-hoc, so a new identifier defines a new list.

id.description: The envelope identifier that would be included in the response (ENVID)

return.description: Specifies if only headers or the entire body of the message should be included in the response (RET)

notify.description: Defines the conditions under which a DSN response should be sent

enumDescriptions.never: Never send a delivery status notification
enumDescriptions.success: Notify when the message is delivered
enumDescriptions.failure: Notify when the message cannot be delivered
enumDescriptions.delay: Notify when the message is delayed

recipient.description: The email address the DSN should be sent (ORCPT)

baseUrl.description: Optional base URL for trackers. This URL must point to your EmailEngine instance.

proxy.description: Optional proxy URL to use when connecting to the SMTP server. A token with restricted permissions can not set this - it redirects a session that carries the account credentials

localAddress.description: Optional local IP address to bind to when connecting to the SMTP server

dryRun.description: If true, then EmailEngine does not send the email and returns an RFC822 formatted email file. Tracking information is not added to the email.
